transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been avoiding part of my job. I can’t really make myself go near the front windows, or that part of the street outside. I keep finding reasons to stay in the back instead.
Are you avoiding the front windows or that part of the street because of a fear or anxiety about something specific, like crowds, heights, or maybe something else?
Not crowds or heights, no. It’s more… that spot. The front windows and the street right outside. I just can’t make myself go over there, so I keep staying in the back and making excuses.
Has something happened at that spot near the front windows or on the street outside that makes you avoid it?

Yeah… something about that spot. I don’t really want to get into all of it. I just know since then I can’t make myself go near the front windows or that part of the street, and I keep making excuses to stay in the back, even though I’m supposed to help up front too.
Can you tell me more about what happened at that spot near the front windows? Did something traumatic or frightening occur there that you still think about when you avoid it?

There was a crash there. I don’t really like talking about it, but… it keeps popping into my head. Like when I’m setting up displays, suddenly I can hear the bang again and see the glass coming down, like it’s happening right then.

latest_inference.note: The patient described avoidance of a specific location (front windows and street outside) and intrusive recollections of a traumatic event (crash with glass breaking) occurring there, consistent with Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder. Other anxiety disorders (e.g., specific phobia, panic disorder) are less likely given the clear trauma-related re-experiencing symptoms. No evidence for other candidates like OCD or adjustment disorder.
